title: Reservation Scaling Handshake: soft-fences, burst metering and rebalancer PRD
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Define and deliver the ‘Reservation Scaling Handshake’ feature: a combination of an automated rebalancer that adjusts reserved-pool allocations, soft-fence (graceful throttling instead of hard-preempt) semantics for tenants that exceed reservations, and an on-chain (tenant-visible) burst metering ledger that tracks credit usage for transient bursts. Goal is to reduce noisy neighbor incidents, enable predictable economics for tenants, and permit safe transient bursts without immediate preemption.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity request reserved pools for stable throughput. We’ve observed two recurring problems: (1) transient spikes cause downstream latency and cross-tenant contention, and (2) overly aggressive preemption creates customer-visible failures. Current reserve allocation is static and lacks a shared accounting of burst consumption. This PRD proposes a coordinated approach: a rebalancer that shifts small amounts of headroom between pools, soft-fence behavior for best-effort bursts, and a burst-credit ledger that powers UI/API metering and billing signals.
goals: Reduce cross-tenant tail latency by 30% in burst windows
Provide safe transient burst capability while preserving reservation SLOs
Expose per-tenant burst credits and burn-rate in Console and API
Allow automated small-reserve rebalances when headroom is idle with operator limits
non_goals: Replace large-scale manual reservations or contractual SLA changes
Real-time market-based billing or auctioning of capacity (phase 2 might explore)
Full multi-cloud brokered allocation — scope limited to Redwood Dedicated clusters
in_scope: Design and implement a rebalancer service that runs on the control plane
Define soft-fence/trickle throttling semantics and enforcement hooks in serving runtime
Burst credit ledger: emit events, store daily aggregates, surface to Console and API
Console UX: tenant burst dashboard, current credit balance, historical burn rate
API: read/write endpoints for credits, and a usage webhook for billing ingestion
E2E tests for graceful degradation, rebalancer decisions, and rollback behavior
out_of_scope: Billing rate changes or invoice-level line-itemization (billing team will implement),
Extending rebalancer to Private/VPC deployments (future work),
Per-model kernel tuning — runtime will expose hooks but kernel work separate
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Rebalancer will shift up to 10% of idle headroom between compatible pools within a zone; shifts are observable in audit logs and reversible

AC2: Soft-fence policy enacted: when reservation is exhausted, best-effort requests enter a prioritized queue with a configurable degrade profile (max wait 800ms, or 50 tokens served at lower concurrency) instead of immediate eviction
AC3: Burst ledger emits per-tenant credit transactions (grant, spend, reclaim) with ISO8601 timestamps and is queryable via API for the last 90 days
AC4: Console shows current credit balance, 7d burn rate, and top 3 burst-producing routes per tenant; values update within 90s of events
AC5: Automated canary deploy shows no >5% regression in P95 latency for non-burst tenants across a 3-hour synthetic workload
AC6: Rollback plan documented and tested: feature flag toggle fully disables rebalancer and soft-fence enforcement within 2 minutes
AC7: Security review signed-off for ledger storage and access patterns (KMS keys for any persisted sensitive metadata)
success_metrics: Metric: cross-tenant tail latency (P99) during bursts reduced by >=25% after rollout
Metric: number of hard-preemptions reduces by >=70% for tenants with soft-fence enabled
Metric: customer satisfaction for Dedicated customers (NPS/CSAT) does not degrade post-launch
Metric: burst credit visibility: 90% of active Dedicated tenants query the ledger at least once in first 30 days
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: (1) Internal dogfood cluster with telemetry and opt-in flag for selected tenants (2) soft launch to 5 enterprise tenants on a whitelist, monitor 72 hours with SRE on-call (3) gradual ramp to 30% of Dedicated clusters with feature flags and automated rollback triggers (4) GA after 6 weeks if KPIs are met.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: soft-fence queue length > 1000 requests for >10m
Alert: unexpected credit negative balance event
Dashboard: per-zone headroom, rebalancer actions per hour, P95/P99 latency by tenant
ui_changes: Console: New 'Burst credits' panel under Dedicated -> Usage
Console: Rebalancer activity feed in cluster operations (audit trail)
Console: Toggle to opt-in/out a tenant for automated rebalances
implementation_notes: Work split across runtime, control-plane rebalancer, and console teams. Rebalancer will use existing capacity measurement signals (headroom meters) and submit signed actions to cluster agents. Soft-fence enforcement will be implemented as a configurable behavior in the serving runtime’s admission path to avoid cascading failures. Ledger writes append-only to a sharded events store; daily rollups written to BigQuery for analytics.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Rebalancer thrashes allocations and causes instability -> mitigation: 30m cooldown and operator-specified min-reserve per tenant
Risk: Bursts accidentally billed incorrectly -> mitigation: emit immutable event stream and mirror to billing pipeline for reconciliation
Risk: Soft-fence increases tail latency for bursters -> mitigation: enforce hard max wait and fallback to immediate low-priority tokens path
open_questions: Q1: Should burst credits be purchasable by tenants (prepaid) or only granted automatically? Decision needed for billing integration.
Q2: What is the canonical set of ‘compatible pools’ for rebalances (same zone only, or cross-zone with warmup)?
Q3: How granular should ledger retention be for audits (90 days vs 365 days)? Cost trade-off to evaluate.
notes: Design review scheduled for 2025-03-12. Early feedback from alpha tenants indicates desire for a per-route burn cap; prioritize as a follow-up. Security to evaluate ledger encryption scope before dev starts.
